extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), third-party requesters, patent owners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for conducting and deciding ex parte and inter partes patent reexaminations at the USPTO, including requirements for requests, identification of a "substantial new question of patentability (SNQ)", office action content, amendments, third-party participation, appeals, and duty of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can request reexamination during enforceability period (can be anonymous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis effective July 1, 1981; request may be by patent owner or third party. Reexamination may only be granted to answer a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) based on patents and printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request Inter Partes Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third party requester can request reexamination during enforceability period; real party in interest must be revealed; must certify that estoppel provisions do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to patents issued from original applications filed on or after November 29, 1999. Inter partes allows right to comment on patent owner responses and right to appeal to BPAI and CAFC (per amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art limitation for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art for reexamination is limited to patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment in 2002 expanded prior art that can support reexamination but the base limitation remains patents and printed publications (applicable to both ex parte and inter partes). See MPEP §§ 2210, 2610, 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ) existence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantial new question of patentability must be present for reexamination to be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is only necessary that prior art reference(s) raise an SNQ for at least one patent claim — i.e., prior art such that a reasonable examiner would consider the teaching important in deciding whether or not the claim was patentable. It is not necessary that a prima facie case of unpatentability exist. Previously considered references may satisfy SNQ if considered in a new light (post-Nov 2, 2002 amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ and prior Office or court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The same question of patentability must not have been decided by the Office or in a final holding of invalidity by the federal courts to preclude SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final court holdings do not control SNQ. Final court holdings of invalidity are controlling (no SNQ for those claims). Different standards between courts and PTO (e.g., In re Trans Texas; In re Swanson): question litigated in court may still be an SNQ before the USPTO because of differing standards and claim construction; previously-considered references may be applied in a new light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on reexamination request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on the request must be made within 3 months from filing date (statutory deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to both ex parte and inter partes requests. If filing-date compliance is met, USPTO must determine grant/deny within the statutory time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of order when granting Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If SNQ exists, the determination will include an order for ex parte reexamination of the patent; the examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the prior art raises such a question with respect to at least one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior notice in the Official Gazette is constructive notice and reexamination will proceed. No rejection of a claim should be included in the order, but all issues identified in the request should be addressed. See 37 CFR 1.525 and MPEP § 2246.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of issues required in the Order
rubrics_metrics.description: For each SNQ identified, the decision should state the prior art adding new teaching, what the new teaching is, the claims the new teaching is directed to, that the teaching was not previously considered nor addressed in prior examination or final court holding, that a reasonable examiner would consider it important, and when priority is raised explain why the prior art is available against patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements must be explicitly stated so the scope and basis of the reexamination are clear. See MPEP § 2246 and § 2646 for ex parte and inter partes respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denying a reexamination request – required explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If no new question of patentability is raised, reexamination is denied and the decision must indicate for each prior art reference why the citation is cumulative, not available against the claims, or not important to a reasonable examiner in determining patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester has one month after the determination denying the request to file a petition under applicable CFR sections for review; a petition decision affirming denial is final and non-appealable. If no petition is filed the reexamination is terminated. (MPEP § 2247, § 2647)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner’s Statement timing and acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If ex parte reexamination is ordered, the decision will set a period of two months in which patent owner may file a statement or amendment of claims (optional). Except as provided, no premature statement/response will be acknowledged in the determination of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a pilot for waiver of Patent Owner’s Statement in Ex Parte Reexamination; Office may consider making permanent. See 35 U.S.C. § 304 and 37 CFR § 1.510(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third Party Requester’s Reply scope and timing (Ex Parte)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester may reply to patent owner’s statement (if one is filed) within two months of owner’s service date; the reply is not limited to issues raised in the patent owner’s statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no owner’s statement is filed, no requester’s reply is permitted. After the reply period, no further requester-filed papers will be considered or entered in the reexam file. (MPEP § 2251; 37 CFR § 1.535)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of Examiner’s First Action on the Merits (FAOM) in Ex Parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s FAOM should be so complete that the second Office action can properly be a final action; it should respond to the substance of each argument raised by the patent owner and requester and, if one or more claims are considered allowable, indicate why the claim(s) are clearly patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2271 and § 1302.14 for reasons for allowance and detailed explanations. The FAOM should develop issues to enable compact prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination provides a complete reexamination of the patent claims on the basis of prior art patents and printed publications; 35 U.S.C. § 112 issues are not raised for original (unamended) patent claims; new or amended claims may be considered for § 112 issues; claims may not be broader than those of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR § 1.552 & MPEP § 2258. Claims cannot be broadened (35 U.S.C. § 305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response periods in Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period of two months will be set for response to Office actions; exceptions (e.g., resulting from a court order or a litigation stay) may set the shortened period at one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2263 for additional exceptions and details on timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time in Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of time must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due; it must be for a reasonable amount of time and show sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR § 1.550(c) applies; provisions of 37 CFR § 1.136(a) are NOT applicable to reexamination. There is a $200 fee for review of a request for an extension of time (37 CFR § 1.17(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper papers and end of third-party participation (Ex Parte)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active participation of a third party requester ends with the third party requester reply; any further submission by or on behalf of the third party requester will not be placed in the reexam file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR § 1.550(g), after the reply period the Office will not enter additional requester papers into the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Action practice in Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The second Office action in the reexamination proceeding is intended to be a final Office action; examiner and patent owner should identify and develop all issues prior to the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period (usually two months) is given for response. A patentability review conference of three people will review a final action before issuance; such a conference is also convened before issuing a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC). See MPEP § 2271.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final (Ex Parte)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of amendments after final follow the standards of 37 CFR § 1.116; amendments after final should be given consideration if they cancel claims, comply with form requirements, present rejected claims in better form for appeal, or if good and sufficient reasons are shown why the amendment is necessary and not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards mirror after-final practice in patent examination; see MPEP § 2272 for details on what will be considered and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Action practice and effect on reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: A timely first response to a final rejection will automatically result in a one month extension of the shortened statutory period (if a notice of appeal has not yet been filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advisory action is delayed, the time period should be extended (e.g., by an additional month) but the response period may not be extended beyond the six-month statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Office Action practice (Inter Partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Office action usually accompanies the order for inter partes reexamination; if all claims are found patentable in the first action, examiner will issue an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP); where one or more claims are rejected, a non-final action is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes uses specific forms and form paragraphs; both patent owner and requester are sent copies. See 37 CFR § 1.935 and MPEP § 2660.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact prosecution objective (Inter Partes First OA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action is intended to be the primary action to establish all issues that exist so that patent owner and any third party submissions should place the proceeding in condition for issuing an ACP in the second Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive reasons for patentability must be given for each determination favorable to patentability. Examiner must address each issue raised by requester as adopted or not adopted, respond to substance of each requester argument, and state why a requester-proposed rejection is not appropriate if not adopted. Clearly set forth each ground of rejection/objection and reasons supporting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner response requirements (Inter Partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is adverse in any respect, patent owner must reply and request reconsideration or further examination; the response must distinctly and specifically point out each supposed error in examiner’s action (general allegations inadequate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner normally given two months to respond. Amendments must comply with 37 CFR §§ 1.530(d)-(k), 1.941, and 1.943. Supplemental responses are not entered as a matter of right except in specified limited circumstances (e.g., cancellation of claims, adoption of examiner suggestions, placement in condition for allowance, correction of informalities). See MPEP § 2666.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner amendments formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification, claims, and drawings must follow 37 C.F.R. § 1.530 and MPEP instructions: entire text of added/rewritten specification paragraphs, entire text of each claim with parenthetical ("amended", "new"), markings per 1.530(f); drawings as sketches showing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims cannot be broadened (35 U.S.C. §§ 305 and 314); no new matter may be introduced (35 U.S.C. §§ 112 and 132); no amendment other than cancellation will be incorporated after expiration; amendments not effective until reexamination certificate issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes third party comments after owner response — timeliness and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: By statute each time patent owner files a response to an Office action on the merits, a third party requester may once file written comments within 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written comments considered received as of deposit date per 37 CFR § 1.8. Limitations on prior art by third party: may only cite new prior art if necessary to rebut a finding of fact, rebut a response, or the art became known/available to requester after request filing date (37 CFR §§ 1.947, 1.948, 1.501). Comments must set forth point or issue, state page of OA/owner response, and present discussion/argument; if not done the comments should not be held defective if examiner can ascertain they address issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) and Right of Appeal Notice (RAN)
rubrics_metrics.description: A response to an ACP is not required; if no response to ACP is filed by patent owner, no third party requester comments are permitted and a RAN is prepared. Patent owner response to ACP triggers third party comment right, may enable amendments/evidence (not entered as matter of right), and a RAN may issue which triggers appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance of RAN triggers appeal rights; each party has thirty days to file a Notice of Appeal. An opposing party who has not appealed may file a Notice of Cross Appeal within fourteen days from an appealing party’s Notice of Appeal. See MPEP § 2672 and § 2673.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination appeals and NIRC / Certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination appeals are decided by a dedicated group at BPAI; upon conclusion a Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) is issued when appropriate; certificates publish the results listing claims canceled, confirmed, newly added, amended, or not reexamined and identify changes to description, disclaimers, and unamended claims held invalid on a final holding by another forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIRC issued where no response submitted, appeals not taken, failure to file appeal briefs, final BPAI decision not appealed, and after federal court appeals complete. See MPEP §§ 2287, 2687, 2288, 2688.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel effect in Inter Partes Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination has an estoppel effect as to the third party requester; requester must certify that estoppel provisions do not apply when filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel prevents certain challenges in subsequent proceedings; the initiation of inter partes reexamination may be prohibited in some circumstances per 35 U.S.C. § 317 and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material to patentability in a reexamination when it is not cumulative to information of record and (1) it is a patent or printed publication that establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability or asserting patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential material may be submitted per MPEP § 724.02. Protective orders and relevant memoranda apply for information covered by protective orders (e.g., TeleCommunication Systems v. Mobile 365 memo). See 37 C.F.R. § 1.555(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting and public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte and inter partes historical statistics and reexamination operational statistics are available on the USPTO web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific web page given: http://www.uspto.gov/patents/stats/Reexamination_Information.jsp (as of slide date). Use USPTO site for updated statistics and operational info.
